commits.message:
fix(edit): a placement's session state is owned by the chain that placed it, and every load releases what that chain ended

Several configs can place one preset and id, and a placement ends only
between two loads of the files that placed it. So each placement-owned key
(drafts, the configure list, the + libraries and their page cursors, and
the configure key's value) now names its owner: the ordered config files
whose merge placed it.

- src/config/placement-keys.ts mints and reads back every family, in its
  owner-free and owned forms. Each read is checked by re-minting.
- The compile stays shared and names keys owner-free. The owner is added
  at one seam (src/renderer/owned-store.ts), built once per render state
  and once per click.
- Every load that does not fail measures each prefix of its chain before
  unplaced cells are dropped. Across every session in the store, it
  releases each key whose owner is one of its prefixes and whose placement
  that prefix no longer holds, and every family key naming no owner. A
  failed load releases nothing. Author menu keys and keys of other owners
  are left alone. Each release logs its session, owner, chain and keys.
- A layout click releases the clicker's ended keys through the click's
  journal, so its undo restores the drafts.
- The raw session store refuses an owner-free family key on get, set and
  setBatch.
- Navigation steps record the owner they were made under, so going back
  in one config never replays a step over another config's keys.

Ticket: brandon-unfiled-3248.gkjx

fix(daemon): a start-time token names the source that read it, and tokens from two sources are never a mismatch (m5bq)

Each token is tagged `proc:` or `ps:`, and the one identity comparison
answers same, different or incomparable: a pair read by two sources, or
missing a start time, is incomparable and judged by liveness alone. So a
live daemon from before the tags is never taken for a recycled pid by the
arbitration, the fork-bomb registry's sweep or the update act, which now
asks the same comparison.

The host's source is settled once from the platform. The liveness fold
carries why it decided into the arbitration's line, so an owner spared
because its start time could not be read says so. A stat line with no
command-name paren reads as having no start time.

fix(daemon): a process identity carries its start-time wherever the kernel keeps one, and a failed lease write refuses the boot (m5bq)

A lease outliving its owner is judged by its owner's identity, so the
identity has to hold up: on Linux the start-time is read from /proc (the
stat's start-time beside the boot id) with no subprocess, and ps stays for
hosts without /proc. Liveness is asked first, so a dead pid is stale with
no start-time read at all, which is the common case after a daemon's exit.

The ownership self-check and the arbitration compare identities through one
function, pid and start-time alike. A lease write that fails refuses the
boot with its reason, rather than serving until the self-check calls the
daemon displaced. The exit test is folded into the one that proves no
removal runs, and the reason the lease stays is kept once, at the write.

fix(daemon): a daemon's exit leaves the socket lease, so a displaced daemon can no longer unlink a newer daemon's lease (m5bq)

Removing the lease at exit was a read and then an unlink of a shared name.
A newer daemon's publish landing between the two was the lease the unlink
took, and an absent lease drains that newer daemon at its next ownership
check and lets the next EADDRINUSE reclaim its live socket. POSIX has no
unlink-if-still-mine, so no removal of the shared name can be confined to
the lease this daemon published.

Publishing is now the lease's one mutation. A lease its owner left names a
dead process identity, which arbitration reclaims as it does an absent
one, and the next publish replaces it. The unused lease path accessor goes
with the removal.

fix(test): the doctor's effect-refresh run waits for the run before it to report

A click while a doctor run is on its way starts none, and one draw between
two clicks does not carry the first run's reading every time, so the second
click was sometimes taken by the run still out and only three runs reported.
The test now waits for the earlier run's row, which its click cleared, before
it clicks again.

fix(git): the daemon's git and forge reads run without the spawning shell's repository variables (38p6)

The detached daemon's environment is whichever shell spawned it, so a
GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE or GH_REPO from a git hook, a `rebase --exec` or a
vcsh shell pointed every session's git and PR read at that shell's
repository.

The process now settles the names once at start (`git rev-parse
--local-env-vars`, plus gh's GH_REPO) and hands them to createDaemon as
data; the daemon builds its one environment without them before anything
reads it, so every launch that inherits it runs without them and a read
asks nothing. A git that fails the ask or answers nothing leaves a fixed
list (git 2.50.1's answer), warned of in daemon.log, as a standing warning
on every bar and in a new `git environment` doctor row, which otherwise
names the dropped variables. plugin install settles its own through the
same function and warns the same way. The Pages site's simulated git
answers the ask.

fix(state): a session id that is an array index is refused at the checkpoint, so no store's recency moves across a save (px80)

The session book, session state and settings history keep recency in a Map
and persist it through a record keyed by session id. A record lists
canonical array-index keys ("7") first, so an integer-like id jumped to the
oldest end on a round trip and the bound could evict it while newest.

The session-id parse now refuses exactly the canonical array indices (an
integer from 0 to 2^32 - 2 in its canonical spelling), naming the id, at every
door: render, subscribe, click, and each file's load, which drops the entry by
name. The files keep their keyed form.
fix(test): the quiet-text sweep draws through a one-session rig, and each row asserts the theme it drew under (s33)
fix(config): the globals resolution reads each selector's pick under its globals row's sessionKey, the key the settings menu writes (s33)
fix(test): the quiet-text sweep draws each row under the theme it names (s33)
fix(daemon): every move of a connection is one transition of its phase, and a frame past the cap is pushed as RENDER_FAILED on a stream that goes on (df7i)
fix(daemon): a connection is one state, reads one frame, and answers an unencodable reply (df7i)
